content: 1. Posaconazole increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when coadministering these drugs. 2. Elvitegravir, being a substrate of CYP3A4, may have its levels elevated when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor for potential interactions. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pravastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, initiate treatment at the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministering with antiarrhythmics. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of protriptyline. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor its response during coadministration with tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and cobicistat. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Quinidine increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Quinidine is a substrate of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and inhibits CYP2D6 and P-gp. Cobicistat is both a substrate and inhibitor of these enzymes and a P-gp inhibitor. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Elvitegravir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. When coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day. Interrupt quizartinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. After discontinuing the strong inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous quizartinib dose. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Regorafenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide (AF) by inhibiting breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) transport. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Coadministration with a BCRP substrate may increase systemic exposure to the substrate and related toxicity. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg orally every other day when coadministered with cobicistat. Monitor for rifabutin-associated neutropenia and uveitis. 16. Elvitegravir increases rifabutin levels, while rifabutin decreases elvitegravir levels. When rifabutin, a potent CYP3A inducer, is used with elvitegravir (with a protease inhibitor and ritonavir), reduce the rifabutin dose by at least 75%. No dose adjustment of elvitegravir is required. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of risperidone. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be necessary upon coadministration. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 24. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 25. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 26. Safinamide increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor BCRP substrates for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 27. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor seladelpar for adverse effects if coadministered with BCRP inhibitors. 29. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Stiripentol is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 30. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dosage reduction for BCRP substrates if adverse effects are experienced when coadministered. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of selexipag. Use caution and monitor closely. Selexipag is a BCRP substrate. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when coadministered with BCRP inhibitors. 32. Tafamidis increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP. Use caution and monitor closely. Dosage adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the selpercatinib dose to 40 mg twice daily if the original dose was 120 mg twice daily, and to 80 mg twice daily if the original dose was 160 mg twice daily. Monitor for side effects. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sertraline. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor its response during coadministration with SSRIs and cobicistat. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of sufentanil with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, potentially leading to prolonged adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 38. Tafamidis meglumine increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP. Use caution and monitor closely. Dosage adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. 39. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. A decreased dose of tramadol may be required. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trazodone. Use caution and monitor closely. Trazodone is a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP2D6, and cobicistat inhibits both enzymes. 44. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor its response during coadministration. 46. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 47. Ublituximab decreases the effects of elvitegravir due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 48. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
